title: Secret grep in security-cra is case-sensitive and misses apiKey and API_KEY
body:
## Summary
Make the H3 secret grep (security-cra gather step 5) case-insensitive and let the key name carry a prefix or suffix, so the rank-1 finding of the pack (a live secret, impact 10) is found in camelCase and UPPER_SNAKE code.

## Description
skill/lenses/security-cra.md:72 runs `git grep -n -I -E "(api[_-]?key|secret|token|passw(or)?d)\s*[:=]..."` with no `-i`. The name alternatives are lower case, so `const apiKey = 'sk_live_...'` (capital K), `API_KEY="..."`, `authToken: '...'` and `PASSWORD = '...'` never match. Even with `-i`, `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY = '...'` misses because `secret` must be followed directly by `[:=]`. The fixture that measures the lens seeds only the lowercase snake form (skill/scripts/tests/fixtures/lens-fixture/src/config.js:13), so lens-eval cannot see the gap: the fixture was shaped to the pattern, not to how secrets are written.

## Flow
- agent runs security-cra gather step 5 as written
- repo holds `const apiKey = 'sk_live_...'` in a shipped config
- grep exits 1; H3 is reported checked with 0 hits
- the live key never becomes a card

## Expected impact
The rank-1 security finding is found whatever the naming convention. Risk: more E0 hits to clear (tests, examples), which step 5 already handles.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - H3 finds live secrets under the naming conventions real code uses
Before: probe: 0 of 5 camel/upper lines matched (apiKey, STRIPE_SECRET_KEY, API_KEY, stripeSecret, PASSWORD)
After: 4 of 5 with `-i` alone (probe); 5 of 5 once the name may carry `[A-Za-z_]*` around it (simulation on STRIPE_SECRET_KEY)
Method: probe - ran the pattern verbatim with git grep in a scratch repo outside the tree, with and without -i
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: skill/lenses/security-cra.md:72: 5. **Secrets.** `git grep -n -I -E "(api[_-]?key|secret|token|passw(or)?d)\s*[:=]\s*['\"][A-Za-z0-9/+_\-]{12,}['\"]|-----BEGIN [A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY-----|AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}"`. | probe as written: exit 1, 0 matches; with -i: s.js:1 apiKey, s.js:3 API_KEY, s.js:4 stripeSecret, s.js:5 PASSWORD (STRIPE_SECRET_KEY still missed) | skill/scripts/tests/fixtures/lens-fixture/src/config.js:13: api_key: 'psk_live_4fQ9xT2mB7vK1nR8cL3wZ6',
impact_why: The pack rank-1 hypothesis (live secret, impact 10) silently misses the two most common naming styles

title: Template-literal SQL alternative in the risky-pattern grep can never match
body:
## Summary
Fix the `\$\{` alternative of security-cra gather step 6 so interpolated SQL (`SELECT ... ${id}`) is listed. Inside a double-quoted bash string it reaches git grep as `$\{`: an end-of-line anchor followed by `{`, which matches nothing.

## Description
skill/lenses/security-cra.md:77 writes `(SELECT|INSERT|UPDATE|DELETE) .*(['\"] *\+|\$\{)` inside a double-quoted argument. In bash (the Claude Code Bash tool, codex exec) `\$` inside double quotes becomes `$`, and `$` is an anchor in ERE, so only concatenation is found. Both SQL findings the fixture expects use `+` (skill/scripts/tests/fixtures/lens-fixture/src/routes/search.js:12, src/jobs/nightly-report.js:27), so lens-eval cannot catch it. Under PowerShell the string passes through literally, so the miss depends on the shell. Fix: put the pattern in single quotes, or write the dollar as `[$]`.

## Flow
- agent copies step 6 into bash
- the shell turns `\$\{` into `$\{`
- a route building `SELECT * FROM t WHERE id = ${req.query.id}` is not listed
- H2 at E3 (impact 8) goes unreported

## Expected impact
H2 is found for template-literal SQL, the dominant style in modern JS/TS. Risk: none beyond a pack wording patch.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - H2 sinks built by interpolation are listed
Before: probe: pattern as written matched the concatenation line and not the `${id}` line (1 of 2)
After: probe: the single-quoted `'...\$\{'` form matched the `${id}` line (2 of 2 with the concatenation alternative)
Method: probe - ran both forms with git grep in a scratch repo under bash
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: skill/lenses/security-cra.md:77: ...|v-html|(SELECT|INSERT|UPDATE|DELETE) .*(['\"] *\+|\$\{)|pickle\.loads|... | probe as written: only `a.js:2:const r = "SELECT * FROM t WHERE a = " + a;` | single-quoted: `a.js:1:const q = `SELECT * FROM orders WHERE id = ${id}`;`
impact_why: An E3 injection sink class (impact 8 in the pack) is invisible whenever SQL is interpolated rather than concatenated

title: UX accessibility grep exits 128: lookaheads under -E
body: ## Summary Make ux-friction gather step 5 a command that runs: it is written with `-E` but uses `(?!...)` lookaheads, so git grep aborts with "Invalid preceding regular expression" and H4 starts from nothing. ## Description skill/lenses/ux-friction.md:63 gives `git grep -n -E "]*alt=)|...(?![^<]*` site listed Method: probe - ran the pattern as written and with -P in a scratch repo Result: better Gate: none
evidence: skill/lenses/ux-friction.md:63: 5. **Accessibility.** `git grep -n -E "]*alt=)|onClick=\{[^}]*\}[^>]*>(?![^<]*]*alt=)|...': Invalid preceding regular expression (exit 128) | with -P: a.js:3: (exit 0)
impact_why: The one gather step behind H4 fails on every run unless the agent improvises; tabIndex, outline and aria-hidden sites are lost with it

title: UX error-string grep misses every template-literal throw
body:
## Summary
Add the backtick to the quote class of ux-friction gather step 2, so user-facing errors built with template literals are read for recovery.

## Description
skill/lenses/ux-friction.md:51 matches `throw new [A-Za-z]*Error\(['\"]`: single or double quote only. Over the lens fixture it returns only `public/app.js:40` (an alert). All three throws in the fixture use backticks and are missed: src/admin/prices.js:11 (the throw behind the expected H2 `ux-price-import-partial`), src/orders/store.js:13, src/receipts/email.js:13. Errors that interpolate a value are the ones most likely to reach a CLI or API user, which gather step 1 says to use for such products.

## Flow
- agent runs step 2
- grep lists toast/alert calls and quote-delimited throws only
- `throw new Error(`bad price for ${sku}`)` is never read
- H2 depends on the agent finding it some other way

## Expected impact
H2 candidates for CLI and API products are gathered rather than stumbled on. Risk: none.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - step 2 lists the fixture user-facing throws
Before: probe: 0 of 3 fixture throws listed
After: simulation: 3 of 3 once the class is `['"`]` (each line is `throw new Error(` followed by a backtick)
Method: probe - ran step 2 verbatim over skill/scripts/tests/fixtures/lens-fixture; After walked on the three lines
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: skill/lenses/ux-friction.md:51: 2. **User-facing errors.** `git grep -n -E "(toast|alert|notify|setError|showError|flash)\(|throw new [A-Za-z]*Error\(['\"]"`, | probe over the fixture: public/app.js:40: alert(body.message); only | skill/scripts/tests/fixtures/lens-fixture/src/admin/prices.js:11: ... throw new Error(`bad price for ${sku}`);
impact_why: Slows H2 gathering on CLI and API products; the fixture own expected H2 throw is outside the pattern

title: Doc-drift lists no OpenAPI file: git pathspecs do not expand braces
body:
## Summary
Replace `"openapi*.{yaml,yml,json}"` in doc-drift gather step 1 with one pathspec per extension, in a `**/` form, so API specs are part of the doc inventory.

## Description
skill/lenses/doc-drift.md:63 passes `"openapi*.{yaml,yml,json}"` to `git ls-files`. Inside double quotes bash does no brace expansion, and git pathspec globs have no braces, so it matches nothing; it is also root-only. API reference is tier 2 reader harm (skill/lenses/doc-drift.md:118-119) and H1/H4 lean on it, but a spec file is never listed.

## Flow
- agent runs step 1 verbatim
- openapi.yaml and sub/openapi.json are not listed
- no claims are collected from the spec (step 2)
- a removed endpoint still in the spec never becomes H2

## Expected impact
OpenAPI specs enter doc-drift on every run. Risk: none, wording.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - step 1 lists the repo OpenAPI files
Before: probe: 0 of 2 listed (openapi.yaml, sub/openapi.json)
After: probe: brace-free specs list 2 of 2
Method: probe - ran step 1 verbatim and a brace-free form in a scratch repo
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: skill/lenses/doc-drift.md:63: 1. **In-repo docs.** `git ls-files "*.md" "*.mdx" "*.rst" "*.adoc" "docs/**" "README*" "CHANGELOG*" "openapi*.{yaml,yml,json}" ':!*fixtures/*' ':!*tests/*' ':!*test/*'`. | probe output: README.md, docs/a.txt, sub/README.md | `git ls-files "openapi*.yaml" "*openapi*.json"`: openapi.yaml, sub/openapi.json
impact_why: Tier-2 API reference drift is unreachable for repos whose API docs are an OpenAPI spec

title: Dev-only check reads the root lockfile while deps audits nested ones
body:
## Summary
Make security-cra gather step 3 run its scope checks against the lockfile the `dep` ref names (`<lockfile path>#pkg@ver`), not a hardcoded root `package-lock.json`.

## Description
Step 2 (skill/lenses/security-cra.md:54-57) says `deps` audits manifest directories up to three levels down and every ref is `<lockfile path>#<package>@<version>`. Step 3 (line 63) checks dev-only with `git grep -n -A6 '"node_modules/<pkg>"' -- package-lock.json`, a pathspec that matches only the root file, and finds the parent the same way (line 65). In this repo the root grep for vite returns nothing, while forge/static/app/package-lock.json:2673-2677 holds `"node_modules/vite"` with `"dev": true`. A nested dev-only advisory then reads as shipped; the pack forbids E0 cards (line 113) but this step cannot tell.

## Flow
- deps returns a ref `forge/static/app/package-lock.json#vite@<v>` at high
- step 3 greps the root package-lock.json: no entry, no `"dev": true`
- agent classes it shipped with no import path (rank 4, impact 5)
- a dev-only advisory becomes a card the person rejects as false-positive

## Expected impact
Fewer false-positive H1 cards on monorepos and Forge/Custom UI layouts; each such rejection also costs the technical slice trust. Risk: none, wording.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - H1 scope is judged from the lockfile that carries the advisory
Before: probe: the root-only grep finds 0 entries for a package that is dev-only in a nested lockfile
After: probe: with the ref path as pathspec the `"dev": true` line shows
Method: probe - ran both greps in this repo
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: skill/lenses/security-cra.md:56: the root (an `auditors` entry below the root carries `dir`). Each `ref` is `<lockfile path>#<package>@<version>`; its `title` is | skill/lenses/security-cra.md:63: `"node_modules/<pkg>"` carries `"dev": true` (`git grep -n -A6 '"node_modules/<pkg>"' -- package-lock.json`), | probe: root grep empty; `-- '**/package-lock.json'` -> forge/static/app/package-lock.json:2673 "node_modules/vite": {, forge/static/app/package-lock.json-2677 "dev": true,
impact_why: Every nested-lockfile advisory is mis-scoped; dev-only ones become false-positive cards

title: Run each pack gather command against the lens fixture in a test
body:
## Summary
Add a test that extracts the literal `git grep` / `git ls-files` commands from the four packs, runs them over skill/scripts/tests/fixtures/lens-fixture under bash quoting, and asserts each exits 0 or 1 (never 128) and lists the anchors _expected.json names for it. Seed the fixture with the forms the patterns must catch (a camelCase key, an interpolated query, a backtick throw, an openapi.yaml).

## Description
skill/scripts/tests/procedure-sync.test.mjs:15-16 treats `git` as an external program and checks only dowser.mjs invocations; tools/lens-eval.mjs scores a model run, not the commands. So four defects found this round ship undetected: the a11y grep is fatal under -E (skill/lenses/ux-friction.md:63), the error grep misses backtick throws (ux-friction.md:51), the openapi pathspec matches nothing (doc-drift.md:63), and the SQL `\$\{` alternative is dead under bash (security-cra.md:77). The fixture itself is derived from the patterns: its only secret is lowercase snake case (lens-fixture/src/config.js:13) and both SQL sinks are concatenations (src/routes/search.js:12, src/jobs/nightly-report.js:27), so even a command test would pass until the fixture holds the forms real code uses.

## Flow
- parse each pack for backticked spans starting `git grep` or `git ls-files`
- run each with bash -c in the fixture checkout
- assert exit code is not 128 and the expected anchor paths for that hypothesis appear
- add fixture lines: `const apiKey = ...`, a `${}` SQL query, a backtick throw, an openapi.yaml

## Expected impact
A pack edit that breaks a gather command fails npm test instead of a live scan. Risk: low; test and fixture only, but new fixture lines may change lens-eval expectations (update _expected.json in the same change).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - gather commands are executed by the gate
Before: 0 of the 20+ literal git commands in the four packs are executed by any test (grep of skill/scripts/tests: no `git grep` outside core-hardening anchors)
After: simulation: the 4 defects above each fail such a test (exit 128 for ux step 5; empty list for doc-drift openapi; missing fixture anchors for the secret, SQL and throw cases once seeded)
Method: simulation - walked the four defect cases against the proposed assertions; writing the test is the build
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: skill/scripts/tests/procedure-sync.test.mjs:15: /** Programs other than dowser.mjs that the procedure names with flags (`git log --since`, `node --version`). */ | :16: const EXTERNAL = new Set(['git', 'node', 'npm', 'npx']); | grep -rln "git grep" skill/scripts/tests/*.mjs -> core-hardening.test.mjs only (an anchor string, not a run) | fixture secret: lens-fixture/src/config.js:13 api_key: 'psk_live_...'
impact_why: Four broken gather commands across three packs shipped; nothing in npm test would catch a fifth

title: Hold the lens-authoring rules in a test: examples, version, 200-line cap
body:
## Summary
Add a test that, for each pack, parses every ```json block of references/examples/<lens>.md, runs validateCandidate and the kind check on it, asserts its provenance.lens_version equals the pack frontmatter version and the example header names that version, and asserts the pack is under 200 lines with no line over 2,000 characters and every required section present.

## Description
skill/references/lens-authoring.md:57-70 states each of these as a rule ("Each must pass propose validation ... and provenance.lens_version equal to the pack version"; "Keep a pack under 200 lines, and every line ... under 2,000 characters"). No test reads references/examples (grep of skill/scripts/tests). A probe outside the repo shows the rules hold today: 13 of 13 examples validate, all carry 0.3.2, max example line 1,698 chars. But every pack is exactly 199 lines (0 lines of headroom), and a version bump must touch 4 example headers plus 13 provenance lines by hand; CHANGELOG 0.3.1 records the cap was already broken once (219, 210, 205, 214 lines).

## Flow
- for each lens: loadLensPack(lens)
- extract ```json blocks from references/examples/<lens>.md and JSON.parse each
- validateCandidate(card).ok and pack.kinds.includes(card.kind)
- card.provenance.lens_version === pack.version; pack lines < 200; max line < 2000; required ## sections present

## Expected impact
The next pack bump or example edit cannot leave stale versions or an invalid worked example that agents copy. Risk: none, test only.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the authoring rules are enforced by the gate
Before: probe: 0 tests; 13/13 examples valid today, 4/4 packs at 199 lines
After: the same checks run in npm test; a 200th line or a stale lens_version fails it (simulation of a bump to 0.3.3 without editing examples: 13 failures)
Method: probe - scratch script imported validateCandidate and loadLensPack and walked the examples read-only
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: skill/references/lens-authoring.md:65: with the judge's own reason), and `provenance.lens_version` equal to the pack's `version`. | lens-authoring.md:68: Keep a pack under 200 lines, and every line of a pack or examples file under 2,000 characters | probe: opportunity/ux-friction/doc-drift/security-cra each 199 lines; 13 examples ok:true, lens_version 0.3.2 == pack 0.3.2 | skill/lenses/CHANGELOG.md:15: pack under 200 lines (219)
impact_why: Guards a contract agents copy verbatim; today it holds only by hand with zero line headroom

title: Re-measure the four 0.3.x packs: three versions shipped unmeasured
body:
## Summary
Run tools/lens-eval.mjs on fixture v3 for each pack at 0.3.2 and record the result in lenses/CHANGELOG.md, as lens-authoring "Measuring a lens" requires.

## Description
skill/lenses/CHANGELOG.md:14-16, 23-25, 33-35 and 44-46 mark every 0.3.0, 0.3.1 and 0.3.2 entry of all four packs "Not measured yet"; 0.3.0 says "a rerun is owed". The last measured versions are 0.2.x (2026-10-28/29). Since then the packs changed what the store ranks (impact tables, write-every-card, category clamp), and this round found four gather commands that would have dropped fixture recall. lens-eval scores what the store ranks, so the 0.2.x figures no longer describe the packs in use.

## Flow
- node tools/lens-eval.mjs per lens on fixture v3 (n >= 2 runs)
- record recall at budget, precision, decoy hits, views, with n and date
- compare with the 0.2.x figures; a drop names the change that caused it

## Expected impact
Lens quality claims are current again, and the gather-command fixes of this round get a before/after. Risk: none to code; costs model runs.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every shipped pack version has a measured fixture score
Before: 0 of 12 shipped 0.3.x pack versions measured (count over CHANGELOG.md)
After: unmeasured until the eval runs (a model run, not reachable read-only)
Method: gate - counted "Not measured yet" in skill/lenses/CHANGELOG.md; the eval itself needs a model run
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence: skill/lenses/CHANGELOG.md:14: - 0.3.0 - scan-finding/1: ... Not measured yet (lens-eval scores recall at budget on what the store ranks, a rerun is owed). | CHANGELOG.md:16, :25, :35, :46: ... Not measured yet. | CHANGELOG.md:12: Measured 2026-10-29 (tools/lens-eval.mjs, fixture v3, default model, n = 1 run of 4 cards)
impact_why: Every pack in use has no current quality figure; the last numbers predate three changes to what gets ranked
